en: 107 As for the gods her allies, who had marched beside her, 108 In fear and trembling they turned tail, 109 They tried to find a way out to save their lives, 110 There was no escaping the mesh that encircled them. 111 He drew them in and smashed their weapons. 112 They were cast in the net and sat in a heap, 113 They were heaped up in the corners, full of woe, 114 They were bearing his punishment, held in confinement. 115 As for the eleven creatures, the ones adorned with glories, 116 The demonic horde(?), who went as flunkies at her side, 117 He put on leadropes, he trussed their arms. 118 He trampled them under, together with their belligerence. 119 As for Qingu, who was trying to be great among them, 120 He bound him and reckoned him among the doomed gods. 121 He took away from him the tablet of destinies, which he had no right to, 122 He sealed it with a seal and affixed it to his chest. 123 Having captured his enemies and triumphed, 124 Having shown the vaunted foe subservient(?), 125 Having brought about Anshar's victory over all his enemies, 126 Having attained what Nudimmud desired, young Marduk 127 Made firm his hold over the captured gods, 128 Then turned back to Tiamat whom he had rendered helpless. 129 The Lord trampled upon the frame of Tiamat,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet IV: Marduk defeats Tiamat
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 131 He cut open the arteries of her blood, 132 He let the North Wind bear (it) away as glad tidings.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet IV: Marduk defeats Tiamat
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 136 That he might divide the brine and fashion artful things. 137 He split her in two, like a fish for drying, 138 Half of her he set up and made as a cover, heaven. 139 He stretched out the hide, assigned watchmen, 140 Them he ordered not to let her waters escape. 141 He crossed heaven, he inspected the firmament, 142 He made it a counterpart to Apsu, the dwelling of Nudimmud. 143 The Lord measured the construction of Apsu, 144 He founded the Great Sanctuary, the likeness of Esharra 145 (In) the Great Sanctuary, the Esharra he had built, (and in) heaven, 146 He made Ea, Enlil, and Anu dwell in their holy places.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet IV: Marduk defeats Tiamat
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 1 He made positions for the great gods, 2 He set up constellations, the star images. 3 He marked the year, drew (its) boundaries, 4 He set up twelve months of three stars each. 5 After he had laid out the plan for the days of the year, 6 He fixed the position of Neberu to mark the (stars’) relationships. 7 Lest any make an error or go astray, 8 He established the position(s) of Enlil and Ea in relation to it. 9 He opened up gates on both (sides of her) ribs, 10 He made strong bolts to left and right. 11 He established the heights in her vitals, 12 He made the moon appear, entrusted (to him) the night. 13 He assigned to him the crown jewel of nighttime to mark the days (of the month), 14 Every month, without ceasing, he exalted him with a crown. 15 “At the beginning of the month, waxing over the land, 16 “You shine with two horns to mark the naming of six days,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 17 “At the seventh day, the crown is [ha]lf.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 18 “At the fifteenth day, you shall be in opposition, at the midpoint of each [month]. 19 “When the sun can see you on the horizon, 20 “Wane at the same pace and form in reverse. 21 “At the day of di[sappeara]nce, approach the sun's course, 22 “On the thirtieth day, you shall be in conjunction with the sun as a double. 23 “I d[efined?] the celestial signs, proceed on their path, 24 “[…] approach each other and render (oracular) judgment. 25 “You, the sun, … shall abjure murder, wrong-doing, 26 “[…] me.”
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 27 W[hen he …] 28 The val[iant …] 29 The sun […] 30 In […] 31 “[Let …] be given to him […] 32 “You and he […] 33 “Let there arise no […] 34 “Let them be complete […] 35 “At the end [of each month …] 36 “Let there be the day of disappearance (of the moon) […].” 37 After [he had …] given the orders, 38 [He made] the plans for day [and night(?)], 39 He made the day […] 40 “Let the year be equal [in days and nights], 41 “At New Year […] 42 “(Another) year […]
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 43 “Let there be regularly […], 44 “The door bolt of … [ ].” 45 After he had as[signed] the days […], 46 [And fixed] the divisions of night and day, 47 […] the foam of Tiamat, 48 Marduk created […] 49 He compacted (the foam) and made it billow as clouds. 50 To raise the wind, to cause rainfall, 51 To make mists steam, to pile up her spittle (as snow?), 52 He assigned to himself, put under his control. 53 He set down her head, he heaped di[rt] upon it, 54 He opened underground springs, they filled up with water. 55 From her eyes he let the Euphr[ates] and Tigris flow out, 56 He stopped up her nostrils, he left … 57 He heaped up distant mo[unt]ains from(?) her dugs. 58 Waterholes he drilled through her to flow out into pools.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 59 He coiled up her tail and tied it as “The Great Bond” (of heaven and earth), 60 […] Apsu beneath his feet. 61 He set her crotch as the brace of heaven, 62 Having spread [half of] her as a cover, he established the earth. 63 [After] he had completed his task inside Tiamat,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 70 He took it away, as the foremost trophy, presented (it) to Anu.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 77 When [the gods] saw, they rejoiced and were glad, 78 Lahmu, Lahamu, and all his fathers. 79 Anshar [embra]ced him, proclaimed he be hailed as “the king.” 80 [A]nu, Enlil, and Ea gave him gifts,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 81 Damkina his mother made cries of joy over him, 82 She delighted him [with] a clean festival robe.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 83 To Usmu, who held her gift for bringing glad tidings,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 90 The Lord listened, still covered with the dust of battle.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 91 […] … 92 With cedar [oil] and […] he anoi[nted] his body, 93 He clothed himself in [his] lordly [rai]ment, 94 The kingly glory, the awe-inspiring tiara, 95 He picked up the mace, he held it in his right hand, 96 […] he held in his left hand. 97 He set […] upon […], 98 He rested his feet on a dragon. 99 The staff of success and authority [he hung] at his side. 100 He […] the […] of kingship, 101 After he [had put on] glory, 102 His netted sack, the Apsu […] awesomeness. 103 He was seated like […] 104 In [his] throne room […] 105 In his cella […] 106 The gods, all there are, […] 107 Lahmu and Lahamu […] 108 Made ready to speak and [said to] the Igigi-gods,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 109 “Formerly [Mar]duk was 'our beloved son’, 110 “Now he is your king, pay heed to his command.” 111 Next all of them spoke and said, 112 “‘Lugaldimmerankia’ is his name, trust in him!” 113 When they had given kingship over to Marduk, 114 They said to him expressions of goodwill and obedience, 115 “Henceforth you shall be provider for our sanctuaries, 116 “Whatever you command, we will do.” 117 Marduk made ready to speak and said 118 These words to the gods his fathers, 119 “Above Apsu, the azure dwelling, 120 “As a counterpart to Esharra, which I built for you, 121 “Below the firmament, whose grounding I made firm, 122 “A house I shall build, let it be the abode of my pleasure. 123 “Within it I shall establish its holy place, 124 “I shall appoint my (holy) chambers, I shall establish my kingship. 125 “When you come up from Apsu to make decisions, 126 “Let your stopping places be here, to receive all of you.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 127 “When you come down from heaven to make decisions, 128 “Let your stopping places be there to receive all of you. 129 “I shall call [its] name [Babylon], ‘Home of the Great Gods’, 130 “We shall hold a ceremony ever after with[in] it, that is, the evening rite.”
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 131 When the gods his fathers heard what he commanded, 132 They … […] 133 “Over all things that your hands have created, 134 “Who has [authority, save for you]? 135 “Over the earth that you have created, 136 “Who has [authority, save for] you? 137 “Babylon, to which you have given name, 138 “Make our [stopping place] there forever. 139 “Let them bring us our daily portions, 140 “[…] our […]. 141 “Whosoever shall […] our tasks that we […], 142 “In this place […] his toil [he shall rest from].” 143 They rejoiced […] 144 The gods […] … them. 145 He who knew […] granted him a weapon, 146 He made ready to speak, enlightened them, 147 … […] his command now, 148 He … […] … the rituals 149 […] them […] 150 And […] … 151 The gods prostrated before him, saying, 152 To Lugaldimmeran[ki]a, their lord, they [said], 153 “Formerly, O Lord, you were our beloved son, 154 “Now you are our King […] 155 “He whose glory saved [our lives], 156 “[… gl]ory, ma[ce] and sce[pter], 157 “Let him make plans, everything demanding skill, 158 “We shall [gladly execute them].”
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet V: the ordering of the universe
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 1 When Marduk had heard the speech of the gods,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 2 He was resolved to make artful things: 3 He would tell his idea to Ea, 4 What he thought of in his heart he proposes, 5 “I shall compact blood, I shall cause bones to be, 6 “I shall make stand a human being, let “Man” be its name. 7 “I shall create human beings,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 21 Let your first reply be the truth! 22 Do you speak with me truthful words! 23 “Who was it that started the war, 24 “Suborned Tiamat and drew up for battle? 25 “Let him be given over to me, the one who started the war, 26 “I shall make him bear his punishment, you shall dwell in peace.” 27 The Igigi, the great gods answered him, 28 To Lugaldimmeankia, counselor of the gods, their lord, 29 “It was Qingu who made war, 30 “Suborned Tiamat and drew up for battle.” 31 They bound and held him before Ea, 32 They imposed the punishment on him and shed his blood. 33 From his blood they (Marduk and Ea) made humankind, 34 He imposed the toil of the gods and the gods (from it). 35 After Ea the wise had made humankind, 36 And had imposed the toil of the gods on them — 37 That deed is beyond comprehension, 38 By the artifices of Marduk did Nudimmud create — 39 Marduk the king divided the gods, 40 All the Anunna-gods, all of them, into upper and lower, 41 He assigned to Anu for duty at his command. 42 Three hundred he posted in heaven for duty, 43 A like number he designated for the ways of the netherworld: 44 Six hundred he made dwell in heaven and netherworld. 45 After he had given all the commands, 46 And had divided the shares of the Anunna-gods of heaven and netherworld, 47 The Anunna-gods made ready to speak,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 48 To Marduk their lord they said, 49 “Now, Lord, you who have freed us from toil, 50 “How may we requite you? 51 “We will make a shrine, whose name shall be a byword, 52 “Your chamber shall be our stopping place, we shall find rest therein. 53 “We shall set up a shrine shrine, we shall reinforce its emplacement, 54 “When we come (to visit you), we shall find rest therein.”
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 55 When Marduk heard this, 56 His features glowed brightly, like the day, 57 “Then build Babylon the task as that you requested, 58 “Let bricks be formed for it, build high the shrine.” 59 The Anunna-gods set to with hoes, 60 One (full) year they made its bricks.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 68 All the Anunna-gods devised their own shrines. 69 The three hundred Igigi-gods of heaven and the six hundred of Apsu all convened. 70 The Lord, on the Exalted Dais, which they built as his dwelling,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 74 The great gods sat down, 75 They set out cups, they sat down at the feast. 76 After they had taken their enjoyment inside it, 77 In awe-inspiring Esagila they held a ceremony, 78 All the orders and plans were made permanent, 79 All the gods divided the stations of heaven and netherworld, 80 The fifty of the great gods took their thrones, 81 The seven gods of destinies were confirmed forever for rendering judgment. 82 The Lord took the bow, his weapon, and laid it before them,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 83 The gods his fathers looked upon the net he had made. 84 They saw how artfully the bow was fashioned, 85 His fathers were full of praises for his handiwork. 86 Anu raised (it), speaking to the assembly of the gods, 87 He kissed the bow, “This be my daughter!” 88 He named the bow, these are its names: 89 ‘Longwood’ shall be the first, ‘May It Be on Target’ shall be the second.” 90 The third name, ‘Bow Star’, he made visible in heaven, 91 He fixed its position in the sky with respect to the gods his brethren.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 92 After Anu had ordained the destinies of the bow, 93 He set up royal throne that stood highest among the gods, 94 Anu had him sit there, in the assembly of the gods. 95 Then the great gods convened, 96 They exalted Marduk's destiny, they prostrated themselves. 97 They laid upon themselves a curse (if they broke the oath),
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 98 With water and oil they swore, they touched their throats. 99 They granted him exercise of kingship over the gods, 100 They established him forever for lordship of heaven and netherworld. 101 Anshar gave him his illustrious name, Asalluhi, 102 “When his name is spoken, we will all do obeisance, 103 “At his command the gods shall pay heed. 104 “His word shall be supreme above and below, 105 “The son, our champion, shall be the highest. 106 “His lordship shall be supreme, he shall have no rival, 107 “He shall be the shepherd of the people of this land, his creatures. 108 “They shall tell of his ways, without forgetting, in the future. 109 “He shall establish for his fathers great food offerings, 110 “He shall provide for them, he shall take care of their sanctuaries.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 117 “Let (these) not be forgotten, let them sustain their gods. 118 “Let their holy places be conspicuous, let their sanctuaries be well built. 119 “Though the people of this land be divided as to gods, 120 “For us, whatever name we pronounce, he shall be our god. 121 “Let us pronounce his fifty names, 122 “That his ways shall be (thereby) manifest, his deeds likewise(?): 123 “(1) MARDUK! Who, at his birth, was named by his forefather Anu, 124 “Establisher of pasture and watering place, who enriches (their) stables, 125 “Who by his Deluge weapon subdued the clangorous, 126 “Who rescued the gods his forefathers in distress.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 130 “He imposed the gods' toil, that they be released. 131 “Creation, destruction, absolution, punishment:
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 132 “Each shall be at his command, they shall look to him.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 133 “(2) MARUKKA shall he be, the god who created them (humankind), 134 “Who granted (thereby) the Anunna-gods contentment, who let the Igigi-gods rest. 135 “(3) MARUTUKKU shall be the trust of his land, city, and people, 136 “The people shall heed him hereafter. 137 “(4) MERSHAKUSHU, angry but deliberative, furious but relenting,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 138 “Deep is his heart, all encompassing his feelings. 139 “(5) LUGALDIMMERANKIA is his name that we all pronounced, 140 “Whose commands we exalted above those of the gods his fathers. 141 “He shall be Lord of All the Gods of Heaven and Netherworld, 142 The king at whose disclosures the gods above and below stand in awe. 143 “(6) NARI-LUGALDIMMERANKIA is the name we invoked, mentor of all the gods, 144 “Who founded for us dwellings in heaven and netherworld in time of crisis, 145 “Who divided the positions of the Igigi- and Anunna-gods, 146 “At his name the gods shall tremble and quake in (their) dwellings. 147 “(7) ASALLUHI is that name of his which Anu, his father, pronounced, 148 “He shall be the light of the gods, the mighty defender,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 149 “Who, according to his name, is guardian spirit of god and land, 150 “And who in mighty single combat saved our dwellings from harm.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 151 “Asalluhi they named secondly (8) NAMTILA, god who maintains life, 152 “Who, in accordance with its meaning, repaired the shattered gods, 153 “The lord who revived the moribund gods by his sacral magic spell,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 154 “Let us praise him as destroyer of the wayward foes! 155 Asalluhi, whose name was called thirdly (9) NAMRU, 156 “The pure god who purifies our ways.” 157 Anshar, Lahmu, and Lahamu pronounced these three of his names,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VI: the creation of humankind and of Babylon
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 1 “(10) ASARI, grantor of arable land, who established irrigated fields, 2 “Creator of grain and flax, who causes vegetation to spring up, 3 “(11) ASARALIM, who is honored in the house of counsel, whose counsel excels, 4 “The gods heed, they learn fear of him,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 5 “(12) ASARALIMNUNNA, the honored one, light of the father who begot [him], 6 “Who implements the decrees of Anu, Enlil, Ea, (who is) Ninshiku, 7 “He is their provider who assigns their portions, 8 “Whose tiara increases abundance for the land.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 9 “(13) TUTU is [he] who effected their restoration, 10 “He shall purify their shrines that they may be at rest, 11 “He shall devise the magic spell that the gods may be calm, 12 “Though they rise in anger, they shall turn [back].
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 13 “He shall be supreme, alone in the assembly of the gods, 14 “No one among the gods shall [make himself equal] to him. 15 “Tutu they called secondly (14) ZIUKKENNA, life of the masses, 16 “Who established the holy heavens for the gods, 17 “Who took control of their courses, assigned their stations,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 18 “Let his deed not be forgotten among teeming humankind, let it be held fast, 19 “Tutu they called thirdly (15) ZIKU, who maintains purity, 20 “'God of the fair breeze, lord of obedience and consent, 21 “Producer of riches and wealth, who establishes abundance,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 22 “Who turned all our want to plenty, 23 “Whose fair breeze we caught whiff of in our great crisis, 24 “Let them ever speak of his glorification, let them sing his praises! 25 “Tutu let teeming humankind magnify fourthly as (16) AGAKU, 26 “Lord of the sacral magic spell, reviver of the moribund, 27 “Who had mercy on the vanquished gods, 28 “Who removed the yoke imposed on the gods who were hostile to him, 29 “Who, to free them, created humankind, 30 “The merciful, whose power is to revive, 31 “Word of him shall endure, not to be forgotten, 32 “In the mouth of the people of this land, whom his hands have created. 33 “Tutu, fifthly, is (17) TUKU, his sacral magic spell shall ever be on their lips, 34 “Who with his sacral magic spell uprooted all the evil ones. 35 “(18) SHAZU, who knew the hearts of the gods, who could examine their innermost, 36 “Who allowed no evildoers to escape from him, 37 “Who upheld the gods’ host, who contented them, 38 “Who subdued the insubmissive, their (the gods’) broad [pro]tection, 39 “Who administers justice, uproots twisted testimony, 40 “In whose place falsehood and truth are distinguished. 41 “Shazu they shall praise secondly as (19) ZISI, who silenced those who rose (against him),
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 42 “Who banished paralyzing fear from the bodies of the gods his fathers, 43 “Shazu is, thirdly, (20) SUHRIM, who uprooted all enemies with the weapon, 44 “Who thwarted their plots, turned them into thin air, 45 “Who snuffed out all wicked ones, as many as came against him. 46 “The gods shall ever hail him in the assembly! 47 “Shazu is, fourthly, (21) SUHGURIM, who ensured obedience for the gods his fathers,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 48 “Who uprooted the enemy, destroyed their offspring, 49 “Who dissipated their preparations, leaving not one of them intact.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 53 “Who brought all the gods who had fled back into their sanctuaries.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 55 “To Shazu, moreover, they shall all render universal honor sixthly as (23) ZAHGURIM, 56 “He it is who destroyed all foes in battle. 57 “(24) ENBlLULU, lord who made them flourish, is he, 58 “Their mighty chosen one, who established offerings, 59 “Who establishes grazing and well-ordered watering places for the land,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 60 “Who opened channels, apportioned abundant waters. 61 “Enbilulu they shall [invoke] secondly as (25) EPADUN, lord of open country and watercourses, 62a “Irrigator of heaven and earth, former of furrows, who formed the pristibe plow land in the steppe, 62b (no English for this line in the eBL edition) 63 “Who regulates dike and ditch, who patterns the furrowed ground.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 64 “Enbilulu they shall praise thirdly as (26) ENBILULU-GUGAL, irrigator of the watercourses of the gods, 65 “Lord of abundance, plenty, high yields, 66 “Producer of wealth, enricher of the inhabited world, 67 “Bestower of grain, who causes barley to appear.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 68 “Enbilulu let them speak of fourthly as (27) HEGAL, who heaps up abundance for the peoples, 69 “Who rains prosperity over the wide earth, who makes vegetation flourish. 70 “(28) SIRSIR, who heaped up the mountain over Tiamat, 71 “Who ravaged the corpse of Tiamat with [his] weapon, 72 “Leader of the land, their faithful shepherd, 73 “To whom have been granted the cultivated field, the subsistence field, the furrow, 74 “Who crossed vast Tiamat back and forth in his wrath, 75 “Passing back and forth, as a bridge, at the place of single combat with her. 76 “Sirsir they named secondly (29) MALAH, so be it,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 77 “Tiamat is his vessel and he the boatman.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 79 “Who brings forth barley and flocks, grantor of the land’s seed. 80 “(31) GILIMMA, who established the bond of the gods, creator of enduring things, 81 “The bridle that curbed them, provider of good things,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 82 “(32) AGILIMMA, the lofty one, remover of the diadem, who controls the snow, 83 “Creator of the earth above the waters, establisher of the heights of heaven. 84 “(33) ZULUM, who assigned fields for the gods, measured off his handiwork, 85 “Grantor of portions and food offerings, tender of sanctuaries. 86 “(34) MUMMU, creator of heaven and netherworld, who guides the lost,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 87 “Divine purifier of heaven and netherworld, is, secondly, (35) ZULUMMU, 88 “To whom no other among the gods was equal in strength. 89 “(35) GISHNUMUNAB, creator of all peoples, who made the world regions, 90 “Who destroyed Tiamat’s gods, who made human beings from parts of them.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 91 “(36) LUGALABDUBUR, the king who dissipated the preparations of Tiamat, neutralized [her] weapons, 92 “Whose support is firm in front and rear.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 93 “(37) PAGALGUENNA, foremost of all lords, whose strength is outstanding,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 94 “Who was greatest of the gods his brethren, lord of them all. 95 “(38) LUGALDURMAH, king of the bond of the gods, lord of the “Great Bond,” 96 “Who is greatest in the royal abode, most exalted by far among the gods. 97 “(39) ARANUNNA, counsellor of Ea, creator of the gods [his] fathers, 98 “Who, for his lordly ways no god whatever could equal.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 99 “(40) DUMUDUKU, who renews for himself his pure dwelling in “Holy Hill,” 100 “Son of “Holy Hill,” without whom the lord of “Holy Hill” makes no decision. 101 “(41) LUGALSHUANNA, king whose strength is outstanding among the gods,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 102 “Lord, strength of Anu, he who became supreme, chosen of Anshar. 103 “(42) IRUGGA, who ravaged all of them amidst Tiamat, 104 “Who gathered all wisdom to himself, universal in perception.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 105 “(43) IRQINGU, ravager of Qingu, ... of battle, 107 “(44) KINMA, commander of all the gods, grantor of counsel,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 108 “At whose name the gods quake for fear like a whirlwind.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 109 “(45) DINGIR-ESIZKUR shall dwell aloft in the house of prayer,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 110 “The gods shall bring in their presents before him,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 111 “Until he receives their due.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 112 “No one but he can create artful things, 113 “The four peoples of this land are his creatures, 114 “No god but he knows how long they will live.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 115 “(46) GIBIL, who tempered(?) the weapons, 116 “Who, in the battle with Tiamat, could create artful things, 117 “Universal in wisdom, ingenious in perception, 118 “Whose heart is so deep that all the gods together cannot comprehend it.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 119 “(47) ADDU shall be his name, the whole sky he shall cover, 120 “His beneficent roar shall thunder over the earth,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 121a “As he rumbles, he shall reduce the burden of the clouds, below, for the people, he shall grant sustenance.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 121b (no English for this line in the eBL edition)
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 122 “(48) ASHARU, who, according to his name, mustered the gods of destinies,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 123 “He has taken all peoples in his charge. 124 “(49) NEBERU shall hold the crossing place of heaven and earth, 125 “They shall not cross above and below without awaiting him,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 126 “Neberu is his star that he made visible in the skies. 127 “He shall stand at the turning point, they shall look upon him, 128 “Saying, ‘He who crossed back and forth, without resting, in the middle of Tiamat, 129 ‘Neberu (“Crossing”) shall be his name, who holds the middle of it.’ 130 “He shall fix the motions of the stars of heaven, 131 “He shall herd all the gods like sheep. 132 “He shall keep Tiamat subdued, he shall keep her life cut short,
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 133 “In the future of humankind, with the passing of time, 134 “He shall proceed unhindered, he shall persevere till distant days.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 135 “Because he created the firmament and fashioned the surface of the earth, 136 “Father Enlil has named (him) his own name (50) ‘Lord of the World’.” 137 When Ea had heard all the names the Igigi-gods had named (him), 138 He was joyful of heart.
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 139 Saying, “He whose name his fathers have glorified, 140 “His name, like mine, shall be ‘Ea’. 141 “He shall be master of the sum total of my powers, 142 “He shall execute of all my commands.” 143 The great gods named his fifty names 144 “The Fifty,” they made his position supreme. 145 They must be grasped: the “first one” should reveal (them), 146 The wise and knowledgeable should ponder (them) together, 147 The master should repeat, and make the pupil understand. 148 The “shepherd,” the “herdsman” should pay attention, 149 He must not neglect the Enlil of the gods, Marduk, 150 So his land may prosper and he himself be safe. 151 His word is truth, his command unalterable, 152 Not one god can contradict what he says. 153 If he frowns, he will not relent, 154 If he is angry, no god can face his rage. 155 His heart is deep, his feelings all encompassing, 156 He before whom crime and sin must appear for judgment. 157 The revelation (of the names) that the “first one” discoursed before him (Marduk),
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: 158 He wrote down and preserved for the future to hear, 159 The destiny of Marduk whom the Igigi-gods exalted, 160 Wherever water is the drink, his name let them invoke. 161 Let them sound abroad the song of Marduk, 162 How he defeated Tiamat and took kingship. 163 [… An]u, Enlil and Ea, Belet-ili […] 164 [… i]n? Babylon [and] Esagila […].
title: Enuma Elish, Tablet VII: the fifty names of Marduk
author: Anonymous (Babylonian)

en: A 1-10 …… sets up ……. "I will …… the perishing of my mankind; for Nintur, I will stop the annihilation of my creatures, and I will return the people from their dwelling grounds. Let them build many cities so that I can refresh myself in their shade. Let them lay the bricks of many cities in pure places, let them establish places of divination in pure places, and when the fire-quenching …… is arranged, the divine rites and exalted powers are perfected and the earth is irrigated, I will establish well-being there."
title: The Sumerian Flood Story (Eridu Genesis): Nippur tablet CBS 10673
author: Sumerian scribes (anonymous)

en: A 10-14 After An, Enlil, Enki and Ninḫursaĝa had fashioned the black-headed people, they also made animals multiply everywhere, and made herds of four-legged animals exist on the plains, as is befitting. (approx. 32 lines missing)
title: The Sumerian Flood Story (Eridu Genesis): Nippur tablet CBS 10673
author: Sumerian scribes (anonymous)

en: B 1-3 (3 lines fragmentary)
title: The Sumerian Flood Story (Eridu Genesis): Nippur tablet CBS 10673
author: Sumerian scribes (anonymous)

en: B 4-5 "I will oversee their labour. Let …… the builder of the Land, dig a solid foundation."
title: The Sumerian Flood Story (Eridu Genesis): Nippur tablet CBS 10673
author: Sumerian scribes (anonymous)

en: B 6-18 After the …… of kingship had descended from heaven, after the exalted crown and throne of kingship had descended from heaven, the divine rites and the exalted powers were perfected, the bricks of the cities were laid in holy places, their names were announced and the …… were distributed. The first of the cities, Eridug, was given to Nudimmud the leader. The second, Bad-tibira, was given to the Mistress. The third, Larag, was given to Pabilsaĝ. The fourth, Zimbir, was given to the hero Utu. The fifth, Šuruppag, was given to Sud. And after the names of these cities had been announced and the …… had been distributed, the river ……, …… was watered, and with the cleansing of the small canals …… were established. (approx. 34 lines missing)
title: The Sumerian Flood Story (Eridu Genesis): Nippur tablet CBS 10673
author: Sumerian scribes (anonymous)

en: C 1-27 ……seat in heaven. …… flood. …… mankind. So he made ……. Then Nintur ……. Holy Inana made a lament for its people. Enki took counsel with himself. An, Enlil, Enki and Ninḫursaĝa made all the gods of heaven and earth take an oath by invoking An and Enlil. In those days Zi-ud-sura the king, the gudug priest, ……. He fashioned ……. The humble, committed, reverent ……. Day by day, standing constantly at ……. Something that was not a dream appeared, conversation ……, …… taking an oath by invoking heaven and earth. In the Ki-ur, the gods …… a wall. Zi-ud-sura, standing at its side, heard: "Side-wall standing at my left side, ……. Side-wall, I will speak words to you; take heed of my words, pay attention to my instructions. A flood will sweep over the …… in all the ……. A decision that the seed of mankind is to be destroyed has been made. The verdict, the word of the divine assembly, cannot be revoked. The order announced by An and Enlil cannot be overturned. Their kingship, their term has been cut off; their heart should be rested about this. Now ……. What ……." (approx. 38 lines missing)
title: The Sumerian Flood Story (Eridu Genesis): Nippur tablet CBS 10673
author: Sumerian scribes (anonymous)

en: D 1-11 All the windstorms and gales arose together, and the flood swept over the ……. After the flood had swept over the land, and waves and windstorms had rocked the huge boat for seven days and seven nights, Utu the sun god came out, illuminating heaven and earth. Zi-ud-sura could drill an opening in the huge boat and the hero Utu entered the huge boat with his rays. Zi-ud-sura the king prostrated himself before Utu. The king sacrificed oxen and offered innumerable sheep.
title: The Sumerian Flood Story (Eridu Genesis): Nippur tablet CBS 10673
author: Sumerian scribes (anonymous)

en: D 12-17 (six lines fragmentary) (approx. 33 lines missing)

en: E 1-2 "They have made you swear by heaven and earth, ……. An and Enlil have made you swear by heaven and earth, ……."

author: Sumerian scribes (anonymous)

en: E 3-11 More and more animals disembarked onto the earth. Zi-ud-sura the king prostrated himself before An and Enlil. An and Enlil treated Zi-ud-sura kindly ……, they granted him life like a god, they brought down to him eternal life. At that time, because of preserving the animals and the seed of mankind, they settled Zi-ud-sura the king in an overseas country, in the land Dilmun, where the sun rises.
title: The Sumerian Flood Story (Eridu Genesis): Nippur tablet CBS 10673

en: 1 King of all settlements, creator of the universe, […]! 2 Hendursanga, first-born son of Enlil, [...], 3 Bearer of the august scepter, shepherd of the black-headed people, herdsman of [mankind]! 4 Išum, zealous butcher whose hands are suited to bear his fierce weapons, 5 And at the lightning of whose wrathful spears even Erra, the warrior of the gods, trembles in (his) abode!
title: Erra and Ishum, Tablet I: Erra roused to war
author: Kabti-ilani-Marduk

en: 6 His heart yearned for combat; 7 To his weapons he exhorted, “Smear yourselves with deadly venom!” 8 To the Seven, peerless warriors, “Gird your arms!” 9 And he said to you, (Išum): “I shall head for the (battle) field!” 10 You alone are the torch, it is your light they look to! 11 You alone are the champion, the gods [march behind!] 12 You alone are the sword, the butcher […]! 13 Should Erra arise, when he destroys the country, 14 Your mind will not rejoice, your heart will not be joyous. 15 Erra, like a sleepless man, his limbs are weary, 16 To his heart he said: “Shall I arise? Or shall I sleep on?” 17 To his weapons he exhorted, “Keep leaning on the corners!” 18 To the Seven, peerless warriors, “Return to your abode!”. 19 Until you should wake him, he is asleep in his bed,
title: Erra and Ishum, Tablet I: Erra roused to war
author: Kabti-ilani-Marduk

en: 34 He exhorted the third: “Let your face be that of a lion so that whoever beholds you melts down!” 35 He said to the fourth: “May the mountain be destroyed at the attack of your fiery weapons!” 36 And then to the fifth he said: “Blow like the wind and overwhelm the world!” 37 To the sixth he commanded: “sweep over above and below, sparing no one!” 38 The seventh he filled with viper’s venom: “Finish (all) life!”. 39 Once Anu had fixed the lot of all Seven, 40 He handed them over to Erra, the warrior of the gods, (saying): “Let them march at your flank! 41 “When the noise of the peoples in settlements becomes unbearable to you, 42 “And your temper drives you to decimate them, 43 “To ravage the black-headed and the wild beasts to destroy, 44 “Let these be your wrathful weapons, that they march at your flank!”. 45 They are furious, their weapons are raised, 46 They turn to Erra: “Rise! Stand up! 47 “Why, like a worn-out old man, do you reside in a city, 48 “Like a little child do you reside in a house? 49 “As one who knows not the (battle) field, will we eat the bread of women? 50 “As if we did not know how to fight, should we tremble and fear? 51 “Going to the (battle) field is becoming for manhood, like a festival! 52 “The city dweller, be he a prince, bread does not satiate him, 53 “Criticized by his own people, despised, 54 “He will have to beg to the humblest soldier. 55 “The city dweller, however mighty his strength, 56 “In what does it advantage the humblest soldier? 57 “The abundant bread of the city cannot compare with the cake baked in embers! 58 “The fine, honeyed beer cannot compare with the water from a waterskin!
title: Erra and Ishum, Tablet I: Erra roused to war
author: Kabti-ilani-Marduk

en: 59 “The palace on the citadel cannot compare with the shepherd’s hut! 60 “Warrior Erra, go out into the (battle) field, rattle your weapons! 61 “Make your noise loud, so that those above and below tremble! 62 “Let the Igigi hear it and extol your name! 63 “Let the Anunnaki hear it and fear the mention of you! 64 “Let the gods hear it and bend for your yoke! 65 “Let the kings hear it and kneel before you! 66 “Let the countries hear it and bring you their tribute! 67 “Let the demons hear it and die for themselves! 68 “Let the mighty one hear it and diminish his strength! 69 “Let the tall mountains hear it and be destroyed, and their summits be leveled! 70 “Let the rolling seas hear it and be troubled, and destroy (their) fauna! 71 “From the thickest forests let its trunks be uprooted! 72 “In the impenetrable reed-bed, let its reeds be snapped! 73 “May the peoples fear and their noise be quieted! 74 “Let the wild beasts shake and be brought to dust! 75 “May your fathers the gods regard and praise your heroism! 76 “Warrior Erra, why have you forsaken the (battle) field and reside in the city? 77 “The wild cattle and the wild beasts have despised us. 78 “Erra warrior, to you we address ourselves: Let our speech be unberable to you! 79 “Before the whole country belittles us, 80 “You must surely hear our advice! 81 “Do a kindness to the Anunnaki, who love silence: 82 “The Anunnaki, because of the noise of the people, are unable to fall asleep. 83 “The pastures – the source of life of the country – are trodden by cattle. 84 “The farmer, over his land, weeps bitterly. 85 “The lion and the wolf destroy the wild cattle.
title: Erra and Ishum, Tablet I: Erra roused to war
author: Kabti-ilani-Marduk

en: 92 Warrior Erra heard them, 93 The words of the Seven pleased him like the finest of oils. 94 He prepared to speak, addressing Išum: 95 “Why, having heard this, are you sitting silent? 96 “Open the path, I shall take to the road! 97 “Let the Seven, the peerless warriors, make war! 98 “Make my fierce weapons march to my flank! 99 “And you, my champion, come before me!”. 100 [When] Išum [heard] these words, 101 Moved with compassion he said, [“alas!”] 102 “Warrior Erra, why have you devised insidious plots against the gods? 103 “You have plotted to ravage the earth and destroy [its inhabitants]; will you not desist?” 104 Erra prepared to speak, 105 Addressing Išum, his champion, in these words: 106 “Išum, pay attention, listen to my words! 107 “Concerning the peoples in settlements, whose pardon you requested, 108 “O champion of the gods, wise Išum, whose counsel is sweet! 109 “In heaven I am a wild bull, on earth I am a lion, 110 “In the land I am a king, among the gods a fury, 111 “Among the Igigi I am a hero, among the Anunnaki a champion, 112 “Among the beasts I am a bowhunter, in the mountain the pit-trap, 113 “In the reedbed I am the fire, in the forest the axe, 114 “In campaign I am the standard, 115 “As the wind I blow, as Adad I thunder; 116 “Like the sun god I oversee the whole orb.
title: Erra and Ishum, Tablet I: Erra roused to war
author: Kabti-ilani-Marduk

en: 130 To Erra, the warrior of the gods, he addressed (his) word: 131 “Warrior Erra! Regarding that action you suggested: 132 “Once, in my anger, I arose from my throne, causing a flood; 133 “I arose from my residence, and the seams of heaven and earth were rent asunder. 134 “The heavens that were shaken: (for this cause,) the celestial bodies changed their positions, and I did not restore them to their places; 135 “The netherworld that trembled: (for this cause,) the (production) of the furrow decreased to such an extent that it was forever difficult to levy (taxes on it);
title: Erra and Ishum, Tablet I: Erra roused to war
author: Kabti-ilani-Marduk

en: 136 “The seams of heaven and earth that were rent asunder: the springs diminished and the floods receded. When I looked again, it was scarcely enough. 137 “The progeny of the living beings was scarce, but I did not restore things; 138 “Till, like a farmer, I took their seedlings in my hand. 139 “I built a(nother) house and settled therein. 140 “My image, which by reason of the deluge was removed, whose appearance was tarnished; 141 “I ordered the fire god to polish my face and cleanse my garments. 142 “When he had polished my image and fulfilled the action, 143 “And I had girded on the diadem of my lordship and returned to my place, 144 “My countenance was haughty, terrifying was my glance! 145 “The people that escaped the flood saw the action fulfilled: 146 “If I should now lift up my weapons, I would destroy the rest. 147 “Those craftsmen I brought down to the Apsû, and I have not yet decreed their return, 148 “I changed the location of the mēsu-tree (and its) amber, and revealed it to none.
title: Erra and Ishum, Tablet I: Erra roused to war
author: Kabti-ilani-Marduk

en: 149 “Now about that action you mentioned, O hero Erra! 150 “Where is the mēsu-tree, the flesh of the gods, fitting for the king of the universe? 151 “The pure tree, the splendid lad, which is meet for lordship; 152 “That in the waters of the vast sea spreads its roots a hundred double-hours to reach the depths of the Netherworld; 153 “Whose top in the heights touches the sky of Anu?
title: Erra and Ishum, Tablet I: Erra roused to war
author: Kabti-ilani-Marduk

en: 128 Shamash made ready to speak and said to the eagle, 129 “You are wicked and have done a deed abhorrent to me, 130 “You committed an abomination of the gods, a forbidden act. 131 “Were you (not) under oath? I will not come near you. 132 “There, there! A man I will send you will help you.” 133 Etana kept on beseeching Shamash day after day, 134 “O Shamash, you have dined from my fattest sheep! 135 “O Netherworld, you have drunk of the blood of my (sacrificed) lambs! 136 “I have honored the gods, revered the spirits, 137 “Dream interpreters have used up my incense, 138 “Gods have used up my lambs in slaughter. 139 “O lord, give the command! 140 “Grant me the plant of birth! 141 “Reveal to me the plant of birth! 142 “Relieve me of my disgrace, grant me an heir!” 143 Shamash made ready to speak and said to Etana, 144 “Go (your) way, cross the mountain, 145 “Find a pit, look inside, 146 “An eagle is cast within it. 147 “He will reveal to you the plant [of birth].”

en: 1-12 Lady of all the divine powers, resplendent light, righteous woman clothed in radiance, beloved of An and Uraš! Mistress of heaven, with the great diadem, who loves the good headdress befitting the office of en priestess, who has seized all seven of its divine powers! My lady, you are the guardian of the great divine powers! You have taken up the divine powers, you have hung the divine powers from your hand. You have gathered up the divine powers, you have clasped the divine powers to your breast. Like a dragon you have deposited venom on the foreign lands. When like Iškur you roar at the earth, no vegetation can stand up to you. As a flood descending upon (?) those foreign lands, powerful one of heaven and earth, you are their Inana.
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 13-19 Raining blazing fire down upon the Land, endowed with divine powers by An, lady who rides upon a beast, whose words are spoken at the holy command of An! The great rites are yours: who can fathom them? Destroyer of the foreign lands, you confer strength on the storm. Beloved of Enlil, you have made awesome terror weigh upon the Land. You stand at the service of An's commands.
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 20-33 At your battle-cry, my lady, the foreign lands bow low. When humanity comes before you in awed silence at the terrifying radiance and tempest, you grasp the most terrible of all the divine powers. Because of you, the threshold of tears is opened, and people walk along the path of the house of great lamentations. In the van of battle, all is struck down before you. With your strength, my lady, teeth can crush flint. You charge forward like a charging storm. You roar with the roaring storm, you continually thunder with Iškur. You spread exhaustion with the stormwinds, while your own feet remain tireless. With the lamenting balaĝ drum a lament is struck up.
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 34-41 My lady, the great Anuna gods fly from you to the ruin mounds like scudding bats. They dare not stand before your terrible gaze. They dare not confront your terrible countenance. Who can cool your raging heart? Your malevolent anger is too great to cool. Lady, can your mood be soothed? Lady, can your heart be gladdened? Eldest daughter of Suen, your rage cannot be cooled!
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 42-59 Lady supreme over the foreign lands, who can take anything from your province? Once you have extended your province over the hills (2 mss. have instead: If you frown at the mountains), vegetation there is ruined. Their great gateways (1 ms. has instead: palaces) are set afire. Blood is poured into their rivers because of you, and their people must drink it (2 mss. have instead: could not drink). They must lead their troops captive before you, all together. They must scatter their élite regiments for you, all together. They must stand their able-bodied young men at your service, all together. Tempests have filled the dancing-places of their cities. They drive their young men before you as prisoners. Your holy command has been spoken over the city which has not declared "The foreign lands are yours!", wherever they have not declared "It is your own father's!"; and it is brought back under your feet. Responsible care is removed from its sheepfolds. Its woman no longer speaks affectionately with her husband; at dead of night she no longer takes counsel with him, and she no longer reveals to him the pure thoughts of her heart. Impetuous wild cow, great daughter of Suen, lady greater than An, who can take anything from your province?
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 60-65 Great queen of queens, issue of a holy womb for righteous divine powers, greater than your own mother, wise and sage, lady of all the foreign lands, life-force of the teeming people: I will recite your holy song! True goddess fit for divine powers, your splendid utterances are magnificent. Deep-hearted, good woman with a radiant heart, I will enumerate your divine powers (2 mss. have instead: good divine powers) (1 ms. has instead: holy divine powers) for you!
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 66-73 I, En-ḫedu-ana the en priestess, entered my holy ĝipar in your service. I carried the ritual basket, and intoned the song of joy. But funeral offerings were (1 ms. has instead: my ritual meal was) brought, as if I had never lived there. I approached the light, but the light was scorching hot to me. I approached that shade, but I was covered with a storm. My honeyed mouth became scum. My ability to soothe moods vanished.
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 74-80 Suen, tell An about Lugal-Ane and my fate! May An undo it for me! As soon as you tell An about it, An will release me. The woman will take the destiny away from Lugal-Ane; foreign lands and flood lie at her feet. The woman too is exalted, and can make cities tremble. Step forward, so that she will cool her heart for me.
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 81-90 I, En-ḫedu-ana, will recite a prayer to you. To you, holy Inana, I shall give free vent to my tears like sweet beer! I shall say to her "Your decision!" (some mss. have instead: "Greetings!") Do not be anxious about Ašimbabbar. In connection with the purification rites of holy An, Lugal-Ane has altered everything of his, and has stripped An of the E-ana. He has not stood in awe of the greatest deity. He has turned that temple, whose attractions were inexhaustible, whose beauty was endless, into a destroyed temple. While he entered before me as if he was a partner, really he approached out of envy.
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 91-108 My good divine wild cow, drive out the man, capture the man! In the place of divine encouragement, what is my standing now? May An extradite the land which is a malevolent rebel against your Nanna! May An smash that city! May Enlil curse it! May its plaintive child not be placated by his mother! Lady, with the laments begun, may your ship of lamentation be abandoned in hostile territory. Must I die because of my holy songs? My Nanna has paid no heed to me (1 ms. has instead: has not decided my case). He has destroyed me utterly in renegade territory. Ašimbabbar has certainly not pronounced a verdict on me. What is it to me if he has pronounced it? What is it to me if he has not pronounced it? He stood there in triumph and drove me out of the temple. He made me fly like a swallow from the window; I have exhausted my life-strength. He made me walk through the thorn bushes of the mountains. He stripped me of the rightful crown (1 ms. has instead: garment) of the en priestess. He gave me a knife and dagger, saying to me "These are appropriate ornaments for you."
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 109-121 Most precious lady, beloved by An, your holy heart is great; may it be assuaged on my behalf! Beloved spouse of Ušumgal-ana, you are the great lady of the horizon and zenith of the heavens. The Anuna have submitted to you. From birth you were the junior queen: how supreme you are now over the Anuna, the great gods! The Anuna kiss the ground with their lips before you. But my own trial is not yet concluded, although a hostile verdict encloses me as if it were my own verdict. I did not reach out my hands to the (1 ms. has instead: my) flowered bed. I did not reveal the pronouncements of Ningal to anybody. My lady beloved of An, may your heart be calmed towards me, the brilliant en priestess of Nanna!
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 122-138 It must be known! It must be known! Nanna has not yet spoken out! He has said, "He is yours!" Be it known that you are lofty as the heavens! Be it known that you are broad as the earth! Be it known that you destroy the rebel lands! Be it known that you roar at the foreign lands! Be it known that you crush heads! Be it known that you devour corpses like a dog! Be it known that your gaze is terrible! Be it known that you lift your terrible gaze! Be it known that you have flashing eyes! Be it known that you are unshakeable and unyielding! Be it known that you always stand triumphant! That Nanna has not yet spoken out, and that he has said "He is yours!" has made you greater, my lady; you have become the greatest! My lady beloved by An, I shall tell of all your rages (1 ms. has instead: daises)! I have heaped up the coals in the censer, and prepared the purification rites. The E-ešdam-kug shrine awaits you. Might your heart not be appeased towards me?
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 139-143 Since it was full, too full for me, great exalted lady, I have recited this song for you. May a singer repeat to you at noon that which was recited to you at dead of night: "Because of your captive spouse, because of your captive child, your rage is increased, your heart unassuaged."
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 144-154 The powerful lady, respected in the gathering of rulers, has accepted her offerings from her. Inana's holy heart has been assuaged. The light was sweet for her, delight extended over her, she was full of fairest beauty. Like the light of the rising moon, she exuded delight. Nanna came out to gaze at her properly, and her mother Ningal blessed her. The door posts greeted her. Everyone's speech to the mistress is exalted. Praise be to the destroyer of foreign lands, endowed with divine powers by An, to my lady enveloped in beauty, to Inana!
title: The Exaltation of Inana (Enheduanna, Inana B)
author: Enheduanna

en: 1 [He who saw the Deep, the] foundation of the country, 2 [who knew all ways], was wise in everything! 3 [Gilgameš, who] saw the Deep, the foundation of the country, 4 [who] knew [all ways], was wise in everything!
title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I: Gilgamesh and the creation of Enkidu
author: Sin-leqi-unninni

en: 5 [He explored] everywhere the seats [of power,] 6 he [knew] the totality of wisdom about everything. 7 He saw the secret and uncovered the hidden, 8 he brought back a message from the antediluvian age. 9 He came a distant road and was weary but granted rest, 10 all (his) labours [were] set down on a tablet of stone. 11 He built the wall of Uruk-the-Sheepfold, 12 of holy Eanna, the pure storehouse. 13 See its wall which is like a strand of wool, 14 view its parapet which nobody can replicate! 15 Take the stairway that has been there since ancient times, 16 and draw near to Eanna, the seat of Ištar, 17 that no later king can ever replicate. 18 Go up on to the wall of Uruk and walk around,

author: Sin-leqi-unninni

en: 54 A triple cubit was his foot, half a rod his leg. 55 Six cubits was [his] stride, 56 [three] cubits the curls at his [cheeks.] 57 His cheeks were bearded, (dark as [gleaming]) lapis lazuli, 58 the locks of his hair growing [thickly as Nissaba’s.] 59 [As] he grew up he was perfect in [his] beauty, 60 by human standards [he was] very handsome. 61 He goes [about] in the sheepfold of Uruk, 62 lording it like a wild bull, [head] held high. 63 He has not any equal, [his] weapons being ready, 64 [his] companions are kept on their feet by the ball. 65 The young men of Uruk are wrongfully vexed, 66 Gilgameš lets no son go free to [his] father. 67 Day and night he behaves with fierce arrogance,

en: 73 ‘[Powerful, pre-eminent], expert, [and mighty,] 74 [Gilgamesh] lets [no] girl go free to [her bride groom.]’ 75 The warrior’s daughter, the [young man’s bride,] 76 the goddess Ishtar was listening to their complaint. 77 The gods of heaven, lords of initiative, 78 [called out to the god Anu] …: 79 ‘Have you bred, indeed, a savage wild bull in Uruk-the-Sheepfold? 80 He has not any equal, his weapons being ready, 81 his companions are kept on their feet by the ball. 83 Gilgameš lets no son go free to his father. 84 Day and [night he behaves] with fierce [arrogance,] 85 he who is shepherd of Uruk-the-Sheepfold! 87 he is their herdsman and they are … […], 88 powerful, pre-eminent, expert, [and mighty,] 89 Gilgameš lets no girl go free to [her] bride-[groom.]’ 90 The warrior’s daughter, the young [man’s] bride, 91 [Anu] was listening to their complaint. 92 They summoned Aruru, the great one: 93 ‘You, O Aruru, created [man:] 94 now create what he suggests! 95 Let him be equal to the storm of his heart, 96 let them rival each other and so let Uruk be rested.’ 97 When Aruru heard this,
title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I: Gilgamesh and the creation of Enkidu
author: Sin-leqi-unninni

en: 98 she fashioned Anu’s idea in her heart. 99 Aruru washed her hands, 100 she took a pinch of clay, she threw it down in the wild. 101 In the wild she created Enkidu, the hero, 102 an offspring of silence, knit strong by Ninurta. 103 All his body is matted with hair, 104 he is adorned with tresses like a woman: 105 the locks of his hair grow as thickly as Nissaba’s, 106 he knows not at all a people nor even a country. 107 He was clad in a garment like Šakkan’s, 108 feeding on grass with the very gazelles. 109 Jostling at the water-hole with the herd, 110 he enjoyed the water with the animals. 111 A hunter, a trapper-man, 112 came face to face with him by the water-hole. 113 One day, a second and a third, he came face to face with him by the water-hole. 114 The hunter saw him and his expression froze, 115 [he] and his herds – he went back to his lair. 116 [He was] troubled, he grew still, he grew silent, 117 his mood [was unhappy], his face clouded over. 118 There [was] sorrow in his heart, 119 his face was like [one who has travelled] distant [roads.]
title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I: Gilgamesh and the creation of Enkidu
author: Sin-leqi-unninni

en: 120 The hunter opened [his mouth] to speak, saying [to his father:] 121 ‘My father, [there is a] certain fellow who has come [to us,] 122 Mightiest in the [land, he possesses] strength, 123 [his strength] is as mighty [as a lump of rock] from the sky. 124 [He wanders always] over the hills, 125 [always] with the herd [do I see him.] 126 [Always] his feet [are found] by the water-hole, 127 [I am afraid and so] I do not go up to him. 128 [He has filled in the] pits that I dug, 129 [he has uprooted] my snares that I laid. 130 [He has set free from my grasp] the herd, the animals of the wild, 131 [he will not let] me do the work of the wild.’ 132 [His father opened his mouth to speak], saying to the hunter: 133 [Go, my son, to] Gilgamesh, [the offshoot sprung from] Uruk’s [midst!] 134 [Make your way] into his presence, 135 his strength [is as mig]hty [as a lump of rock from the sky.] 136 [Take the road, set] your face [toward Uruk,] 137 […] the strength of a man! 138 [Go, my son], bring [with you Šamhat the harlot,] 139 [her allure is a match] for even the mighty! 140 [When the herd comes] down [to] the water-hole,
title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I: Gilgamesh and the creation of Enkidu

en: 141 [she should strip off] her [clothing to reveal] her charms. 142 [He will see] her and will go up [to] her, 143 his herd will be estranged from him, [though he grew up] in its presence. 144 [Paying heed] to the advice of his father, 155 He has filled in the pits that I dug, 156 he has uprooted my snares [that I laid.] 157 He has released from my grasp the herds, the animals [of the] wild, 158 he will not let me do the work [of the] wild.’ 159 Gilgameš said to him, to the hunter: 160 ‘Go, O hunter, take with you Šamḫat the harlot. 161 When the herd comes down to the water-hole, 162 she should strip off her clothing to reveal her charms. 163 He will see her and will go up to her, 164 his herd will be estranged from him, though he grew up in its presence.’ 165 Off went the hunter, he took with him Šamḫat the harlot, 166 they set out on the road, they started the journey. 167 On the third day they arrived at the destination; 168 the hunter and the harlot sat down to wait. 169 One day, a second day, they sat by the water-hole, 170 (then) the herd arrived to drink at the water-hole.
title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I: Gilgamesh and the creation of Enkidu

en: 171 The animals arrived, they enjoyed the water, 172 and also Enkidu himself, whose birth-place was the hills. 173 Feeding on grass with the very gazelles, 174 jostling at the water-hole with the herd, 175 he enjoyed the water with the animals. 176 (Then) Šamḫat saw him, the man-savage, 177 a murderous fellow from the midst of the wild. 178 ‘This is he, Šamḫat! Uncradle your bosom; 179 bare your sex so he may take in your charms! 180 Do not show fear, take in his scent! 181 He will see you and he will come up to you. 182 Spread your clothing so he may lie on you, 183 treat the man to the work of a woman! 184 his herd will be estranged from him, though he grew up in its presence. 185 His ‘love’ will caress and embrace you, 186 Šamḫat let loose her skirts, 187 she bared her sex and he took in her charms. 188 She showed no fear, she took in his scent: 189 she spread her clothing and he lay upon her. 190 She treated the man to the work of a woman, 191 his ‘love’ caressed and embraced her. 192 For six days and seven nights Enkidu, erect, did couple with Šamḫat. 193 After he was sated with her delights, 194 he turned his face toward his herd.
title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I: Gilgamesh and the creation of Enkidu
author: Sin-leqi-unninni

en: 195 The gazelles saw Enkidu and they started running, 196 the animals of the wild moved away from his person. 197 Enkidu had defiled his body so pure, 198 his legs stood still, though his herd was on the move. 199 Enkidu was diminished, his running was not as before, 200 but he had reason, he [was] wide of understanding. 201 He came back and sat down at the feet of the harlot, 202 watching the harlot, (observing) her features. 203 Then his ears heard what the [harlot] was speaking, 204 [as the harlot] said to him, to Enkidu: 205 ‘You are handsome, Enkidu, you are just like a god, 206 why with the animals do you range through the wild? 207 Come, I will lead you to Uruk-the-Sheepfold, 208 to the sacred temple, the dwelling of Anu and Ištar! 209 where Gilgameš is perfect in strength, 210 and lords it over the menfolk like a wild bull! 211 She talked to him and what she said found favour, 212 his heart (now) wise was seeking a friend. 213 Enkidu said to her, to the harlot: 214 ‘Come, Šamḫat, take me along 215 to the sacred temple, the holy dwelling of Anu and Ištar, 216 where Gilgameš is perfect in strength, 217 and lords it over the menfolk like a wild bull! 218 I will challenge him, for [my strength] is mighty,
title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I: Gilgamesh and the creation of Enkidu
author: Sin-leqi-unninni

en: 219 [I will vaunt] myself in Uruk, (saying) “I am the mightiest!” 220 [there] I shall change the way things are ordered, 221 [the one] born in the wild is mighty, he has strength.’ 222 ‘Let [the people] see your face, 223 […that] exists I know indeed. 224 Go, Enkidu, to Uruk-the-Sheepfold, 225 where the young men are girt with waistbands. 226 Every day [in Uruk] a festival is held, 227 where the drums are repeatedly beaten, 228 and the harlots are comely of figure, 229 graced with charm, full of joy. 230 Even the aged they rouse from their beds! 231 O Enkidu, [who do not (yet)] know life – 232 I will show you Gilgameš, the man so merry, 233 look at him, regard his face! 234 He is fair in manhood, he has dignified bearing, 235 his whole person is graced with charm. 236 He has a strength more mighty than you, 237 he is unsleeping by day and by night. 238 O Enkidu, get rid of your sinful intention, 239 as for Gilgameš Šamaš loves him.
title: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet I: Gilgamesh and the creation of Enkidu

en: 240 Anu, Enlil and Ea broadened his wisdom: 241 even before you came from the uplands, 242 Gilgameš in Uruk was having dreams about you: – 243 Gilgameš arose to reveal a dream, saying to his mother: 244 “O mother, the dream that I saw in the course of this night – 245 the stars of the heavens appeared before me, 246 like a lump of rock from the sky one fell towards me. 249 The land of Uruk was standing around [it], 250 [the land was gathered] about it. 251 A crowd [was jostling] before [it], 252 [the menfolk were] thronging around it. 253 They were kissing its feet [like a little] baby’s; 254 [I loved it] like a wife and I caressed and embraced it. 255 [I picked it up and] set it down at [your] feet, 256 [and you, you] made it my equal.” 257 [The mother of Gilgameš] was clever, she was wise, she knew everything, she said to her son; 258 [Wild-Cow] Ninsun was clever, she was wise, she knew everything, she said to Gilgameš: 259 “The stars of heaven [appeared] before you, 260 [like a] lump of rock from the sky one fell toward you. 261 You picked it up but it was too much for you,

en: 218a In order to keep the cedars safe, 219a Enlil made it his destiny to be the terror of the people: 221 Ḫumbaba, his voice is the Deluge, 222 his speech is fire, his breath is death. 223 He hears his forest’s murmur for sixty leagues; 224 who is there that would venture into his forest? 227 In order to keep the cedars safe, 228 Enlil made it his destiny to be the terror of the people. 229 And he who ventures into his forest, feebleness will seize him!’ 230 Gilgameš opened his mouth to speak, saying to Enkidu: 232 Why, my friend, do you speak like a weakling? 233 With your feeble talk you have vexed my heart!

en: 1 ‘[Come back in safety] to [the quay of] Uruk! 2 Do not trust, O Gilgameš, in the fullness of your strength, 3 let your eyes be satisfied, strike a blow to rely on! 4 “He who goes in front saves (his) comrade, 5 he who knew the road protected his friend.” 6 Let Enkidu go in front of you, 7 he knows the way to the Forest of Cedar! 8 He is tried in battles and experienced in combat, 9 let Enkidu protect (his) friend and keep safe (his) comrade! 10 let him bring his person back to his wives! 11 In this our assembly we hereby give the king into your care: 12 you will ensure (his) return and give the king into our care.’ 13 Gilgameš opened his mouth to speak, 14 saying to Enkidu: 15 ‘Come, my friend, let us go to Egal-maḫ, 16 into the presence of the great Queen Ninsun! 17 Ninsun is clever, she is wise, she knows everything, 18 she will set steps of (good) counsel for our feet.’ 19 They took each other hand in hand, 20 Gilgameš and Enkidu, as they went to Egal-maḫ. 21 Into the presence of the great Queen Ninsun, 22 Gilgameš arose and entered before [the goddess, his mother.] 24 ‘O Ninsun, I have grown so bold [as to travel] 25 the distant path to where Ḫumbaba is. 26 I shall face a battle that I do not know, 27 I shall ride a road that I do not know. 28 I hereby beseech you, give me your blessing, so that I may go,

en: 31 I will return and perform the akītu-festival twice in the year, 32 the akītu I will perform twice in the year. 33 Let the akītu take place and the merriment begin, 34 let the drums be beaten in your presence!’ 35 [Wild-Cow] Ninsun was listening in sorrow 36 to the words of Gilgameš, her son, and Enkidu.

en: 87 ‘[O mountain], bring me a dream, so I may see [a favourable message from Šamaš!]’ 88 [Enkidu] made for him [a] ‘house of Zaqīqu’, 89 [he fixed] a storm-door in its doorway. 90 [in the circle he had] drawn he made him lie down, 91 [and falling flat] like a net lay himself in the doorway. 92 Gilgamesh rested his chin on his knees, 93 the sleep that spills over people fell upon him. 94 [In the] middle watch (of the night) he reached his sleep’s end, 95 he arose to talk to his friend: 96 ‘My friend, did you not call me? Why am I awake? 97 Did you not touch me? Why am I in confusion? 98 Did a god not pass by? Why is my flesh benumbed? 99 My friend, I have seen a third dream, 100 and the dream that I saw was completely confused. 101 The heavens cried aloud, while the earth was rumbling, 102 the day grew still, darkness went forth. 103 Lightning flashed down, fire broke out, 104 [flames] kept flaring up, death kept raining down. 105 The fire so bright dimmed and went out, 106 [the flames] diminished and turned into cinders. 107 [You were] born in the wild, can we take counsel?’ 108 Enkidu [heard the words of his friend,] making his dream meaningful to him, he said to Gilgameš: 109 ‘[My friend,] your dream is good, [its message] is lucky.’

en: 1 They stood marvelling at the forest, 2 gazing at the lofty cedars, 3 gazing at the forest’s entrance – 4 Where Ḫumbaba came and went there was a track, 5 the paths were in good order and the way was well trodden. 6 They were gazing at the Cedar Mountain, 7 the dwelling of the gods, the throne-dais of the goddesses, 8 [on the] very face of the mountain the cedar was proffering its abundance, 9 sweet was its shade, full of delight. 10 [Thick] tangled was the thorn, the forest a shrouding canopy, 11 cedars and gum trees, [all entwined,] left no way in. 12 For a league on all sides cedars [lifts up] saplings, 13 cypresses [grew thick] for two-thirds of a league. 14 Cedars scabbed with resin grew sixty cubits high, 15 the resin [oozed] forth, drizzling down like rain, 16 [flowing freely] for ravines to bear away. 17 [Through] all the forest a bird began to sing, 18 [hen birds] gave answer, a constant din was the noise. 19 [A solitary] tree-cricket set off a noisy chorus,

en: 28 [terror] fell on Gilgameš. 29 [Stiffness took] a grip on his arms, 30 and tremors beset his legs. 31 [Enkidu] opened his mouth to speak, saying to Gilgameš: 32 ‘[Let us go deep] into the midst of the forest, 33 [let us get] going and raise a loud cry!’ 34 [Gilgameš] opened his mouth to speak, saying to Enkidu: 35 ‘[Why,] my friend, do we tremble like cowards, 36 [we who] came across all the mountains? 37 ‘[Shall] … before us? 38 Before we have withdrawn… 39 ‘My [friend] is one who is tested in combat, 40 one who has been in battle has no fear of death. 41 ‘You have been splashed in blood, so you need not fear death: 42 [go] berserk, like a dervish fall into a frenzy. 43 Let [your shout] boom loud [like] a kettle drum, 44 may stiffness leave your arms, the tremors depart from your legs!’ 45 ‘Take my hand, friend, and we shall go [on] together, 46 [let] your thoughts dwell on combat! 47 Forget death and [seek] life! 48 [The one who] walks alongside is the prudent man. 49 ‘“[Let him who] goes first be on guard for himself and bring his comrade to safety!” 50 It is they made a name [for days] long in the future!’ 51 [At the] distant … they both arrived, 52 [they ceased] their talking and came to a halt. 53 They stood marvelling at the forest, 54 […]

en: 1 He washed his matted hair, he cleaned his equipment, 2 he shook his locks down over his back. 3 He cast aside his dirty things, he clothed himself with his clean things, 4 He wrapped himself in cloaks, tied with a sash.

en: 5 Gilgameš put on his crown. 6 The lady Ištar looked covetously on the beauty of Gilgameš: 7 ‘Come, Gilgameš, you be the bridegroom! 8 Grant me your fruits, I insist! 9 You shall be my husband and I will be your wife! 10 Let me harness for you a chariot of lapis lazuli and gold, 11 whose wheels are gold and whose horns are amber. 12 You shall have in harness “storm-lions”, huge mules. 13 Come into our house with scents of cedar! 14 When you come into our house, 15 doorway and throne shall kiss your feet. 16 Kings, courtiers and nobles shall be bowed down beneath you, 17 Produce of mountain and lowland they shall bring you as tribute! 18 Your nanny goats shall bear triplets and your ewes twins, 19 your donkey foal under load shall outpace a mule. 20 At the chariot your horse shall gallop majestically, 21 at the yoke your ox shall acquire no rival. 22 [Gilgameš] opened his mouth to speak, 23 [saying] to the lady Ištar: 24 ‘[If indeed I were] to take you in marriage, 25 [...] myself and my clothing, 26 [whence will come] my food and my sustenance? 27 [will you feed me] bread fit for a god? 28 [will you pour me ale] fit for a king? 29 [...] should I bind, 30 […] should I pile high? 31 [Would…] wrap […] in a cloak? 32 ‘[Why] would I take you in marriage? 33 [You, a frost] that congeals no ice, 34 a slatted door [that does not] block breeze and draught,

en: 45 As for him of… […] his arm. 46 To Dumuzi the husband of your youth, 47 to him you have allotted perpetual weeping, year on year. 48 You loved the speckled allallu-bird, 49 you struck him and broke his wing, 50 (now) he stands in the woods crying “My wing!” 51 You loved the lion, perfect in strength, 52 seven and seven pits you have dug for him. 53 You loved the horse, famed in battle, 54 to him you have allotted whip, spurs and lash. 55 To him you have allotted a seven-league gallop, 56 to him you have allotted muddy water to drink. 57 To his mother Silili you have allotted perpetual weeping. 58 You loved the shepherd, the grazier, the herdsman, 59 who regularly piled up for you (bread baked in) embers, 60 slaughtering kids for you every day. 61 You struck him and turned him into a wolf, 62 so his own shepherd boys drive him away, 63 and his dogs take bites at his thighs. 64 You loved Išullānu, your father’s gardener,

en: 113 Anu heard this speech of Ištar, 114 [and] he placed in her hands the nose-rope of the Bull of Heaven. 115 [Down came] Ištar, leading it onward: 116 when [it] reached the [land] of Uruk, 117 it dried up the woodland, the marshland and the reeds, 118 it went down to the river, (the level of) the river was reduced by seven cubits. 119 At the snort of the Bull of Heaven a pit opened up, 120 a hundred men of Uruk all fell into it.

en: 121 At its second snort a pit opened up, 122 two hundred men of Uruk all fell into it. 123 At its third snort a pit opened up, 124 Enkidu fell in up to [his] waist. 125 Enkidu sprang out and seized the Bull of Heaven by [its] horns; 126 the Bull of Heaven spat slaver at his face, 127 [flicking] its dung with the tuft of its tail. 128 Enkidu opened his mouth [to speak,] 129 saying to Gilgameš: 130 ‘My friend, we vaunted ourselves [in our] city, 131 how shall we make amends for the piled-up people?

en: 145 Then Gilgameš like a butcher [(…)], brave and skilful, 146 [pressed home] his knife between the yoke of the horns and the slaughter-spot. 147 After they had slain the Bull of Heaven, 148 they took its heart and set it before Šamaš. 149 They stepped back and prostrated themselves before Šamaš, 150 both of them (then) sat down together. 151 Ištar went up on to the wall of Uruk-the-Sheepfold, 152 she hopped and stamped, she uttered a woeful wail: 153 ‘Woe to Gilgameš, who vilified me, (who) killed the Bull of Heaven!’ 154 Enkidu heard this speech of Ištar, 155 he tore a haunch off the Bull of Heaven and threw it down before her. 156 ‘You too, had I caught you, I would have treated you like it! 157 I would have draped its guts on your arms!’ 158 Ištar assembled the courtesans, prostitutes (and harlots), 159 she instituted mourning over the Bull of Heaven’s haunch. 160 Gilgameš summoned the craftsmen, all the smiths, 161 for the craftsmen to praise the thickness of its horns. 162 Thirty minas of lapis lazuli each was their mass, 163 Two minas each their rims, 164 six kor of oil was the capacity of both. 165 He dedicated (them) for the anointing of his god, Lugalbanda, 166 he took (them) in and hung (them) in his bed-chamber. 167 They washed their hands in the River Euphrates, 168 they took each other (by the hand) to go forward. 169 As they drove along the street of Uruk,

en: 69 [‘My friend, …] … […] manifest, 70 [do you, who] had understanding and reason, [now speak] madness? 71 Why, my friend, did your heart talk profanities […?] 72 [the dream] was precious and the apprehension was much. 73 [your feverish lips] were buzzing like flies, 74 [the misgivings were] great, the dream was rare. 75 “To the one who survived grieving was left, 76 the [deceased] left sorrow to the one who survived.” 77 [I will] beseech the great gods and entreat them, 78 I will seek out [Šamaš], I will appeal to your god. 79 ‘In [your presence] I will pray [to Anu,] father of the gods, 80 [May] Enlil, the great counsellor, [hear my] prayers in your presence, 81 may [my entreaty find favour with Ea!]
